source.title: The Architecture of Open Source Applications (Volume 2) Scalable Web Architecture and Distributed Systems

supporting_quote:
Enter queues. A queue is as simple as it sounds: a task comes in, is
added to the queue and then workers pick up the next task as they have
the capacity to process it.
explanation: The source connects queued processing to worker capacity. The hypothetical messaging system adds an invented 100-message limit, admission rejection, retry backoff, and accepted-message preservation; these are not source-system facts.

flows: Clients submit messages to the admission service.
Workers process queued messages.

rule_reason: Overload may discard messages already accepted successfully.
